title: "My first weeks in MDS"
description: "Orientation, the first week of classes, and what actually surprised me about the pace."

---

Orientation week was mostly logistics — accounts, laptops, a room full of people
introducing themselves — but the part that stuck with me was how quickly the cohort
stopped being strangers. Everyone had arrived from somewhere different: economics,
biology, engineering, a few people coming back after years of work. I had half
expected a room of computer science graduates like me, and instead spent the week
being reminded that most of the interesting questions in this field come from
somewhere other than the code.

Then classes started, and the pace was the real surprise. I knew MDS was compressed;
I had not internalised what a block schedule feels like from the inside. A topic is
introduced, you use it in a lab two days later, and by the following week it is
assumed knowledge. The instinct I brought from my undergraduate degree — read
everything first, then start — stopped working almost immediately. What replaced it
was starting before I felt ready and letting the gaps show up in the error messages.

A few weeks in, I have settled somewhere between overwhelmed and genuinely enjoying
it. The tooling side has been the easiest to love: Git, the shell, and Quarto have
already replaced a pile of habits I did not realise were slowing me down, and this
site is a direct result of that. The statistics is where I am working hardest, which
is exactly why I came. Ask me again after the first round of quizzes.
